title: Relative Picard algebraic space for a cohomologically trivial proper family
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a flat proper morphism of schemes of finite presentation [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Write $X_T=X\times_ST$ and $f_T:X_T\to T$ for every $S$-scheme $T$ [def-pc-base-change]. Assume that the canonical map $\mathcal O_T\to(f_T)_*\mathcal O_{X_T}$ is an isomorphism for every $T$. The fppf relative Picard sheaf $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/S}$ [def-pc-picard-functor] is represented by an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space] locally of finite presentation over $S$. Its diagonal is representable by immersions. Tensor product, the trivial module and dualization of invertible modules [def-sc-invertible-module] give it a commutative group structure. Local finite presentation and immersions of algebraic spaces are tested on etale scheme charts, with local finite presentation as in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; finite presentation for $f$ includes quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness.

source.place: Tags 0D2C (proposition-pic-functor), 0D2D (lemma-diagonal-pic); local finite presentation from 08KD (lemma-coherent-limits), 0D03 (lemma-picard-stack-open-in-coh), and 04AK (spaces-limits.tex, proposition-characterize-locally-finite-presentation). No relative-dimension bound is assumed.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal B_f(T)$ be the groupoid of invertible modules on $X_T$, with arrows the pullback isomorphisms. By [lem-sfb-coherent-stack-algebraic-lfp], the stack $\mathcal C_f$ of finitely presented quasi-coherent modules flat over the test scheme with proper support is algebraic and locally of finite presentation over $S$: properness of $f$ includes separatedness, and its other hypotheses are precisely ours. By [lem-sfb-invertible-open-in-coherent-stack], the inclusion $\mathcal B_f\to\mathcal C_f$ is representable by open immersions. Applying [lem-sfb-open-stack-algebraic-lfp] makes $\mathcal B_f$ an algebraic stack locally of finite presentation over $S$. This argument uses no relative-dimension bound.

source.place: Tags 0D03, lemma-picard-stack-open-in-coh, and 0D04, proposition-pic; moduli.tex Tag 0DMB, lemma-pic-qs-lfp

proof.text: For an invertible module $L$ on $X_T$, multiplication identifies its automorphisms with $\Gamma(X_T,\mathcal O_{X_T})^\times$: on a trivializing open an endomorphism is a scalar, and these scalars agree on overlaps. The assumed canonical isomorphism $\mathcal O_T\simeq(f_T)_*\mathcal O_{X_T}$ identifies this group naturally with $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)^\times$, compatibly with every further base change. Thus the inertia projection of $\mathcal B_f$ pulls back at $L$ to $\mathbf G_{m,T}\to T$. On $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ this is $\operatorname{Spec}(A[z,w]/(zw-1))\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, which has finite presentation. For a square-zero surjection $R'\to R$, lift a unit and its inverse to $a,b\in R'$. Write $ab=1+i$ with $i^2=0$; then $b(1-i)$ is an inverse for $a$. Hence all affine first-order lifting problems have solutions, so this scheme is smooth by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Smoothness implies flatness and local finite presentation by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. These are local on the open affine cover of $T$ by the same cited calculus. Consequently the inertia is representable, flat and locally of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 0DNH, lemma-pic-inertia; examples-stacks.tex Tag 0375, example-inertia-stack-of-picard; explicit square-zero unit lift

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-flat-inertia-algebraic-space-quotient] to $\mathcal B_f$. Its isomorphism-class presheaf is exactly $T\mapsto\operatorname{Pic}(X_T)$, so its fppf sheafification is $P=\operatorname{Pic}_{X/S}$ by [def-pc-picard-functor]. Therefore $P$ is an algebraic space. Work on the big fppf site in a containing universe as in [def-pc-fppf-site]. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local], every section of $P$ locally has a bundle representative and equality of two bundle classes in $P$ is locally an isomorphism of the bundles. These two assertions say exactly that $\pi:\mathcal B_f\to P$ is a gerbe: each fibre has objects locally, and any two fibre objects are locally isomorphic. Choose a smooth surjective atlas $U\to\mathcal B_f$ whose composite $U\to S$ is locally of finite presentation, available from step 1. By [lem-sfb-gerbe-smooth-universal-homeomorphism], its composite $U\to P$ is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. Apply the source-locality clause of [lem-sfb-representable-fppf-etale-open-descent] to the map of algebraic spaces $P\to S$, using the identity cover of $S$ and the cover $U\to P$. Since $U\to S$ is locally of finite presentation, so is $P\to S$.

source.place: Paragraph after Tag 0D2C, proposition-pic-functor, describing the gerbe proof; stacks-morphisms.tex Tags 06QJ, 06QD and 0DN8; spaces-descent.tex Tag 06EV

proof.text: Tensor product, the trivial bundle and dualization induce multiplication, identity and inversion on $T\mapsto\operatorname{Pic}(X_T)$. For sheaf sections, use the local representatives from step 3, pass to a common fppf refinement, and apply these operations there. Changing representatives gives locally isomorphic bundles, hence equal sheaf classes. Thus the results agree on overlaps and glue uniquely. Associativity, commutativity, identity and inverse equations hold on the same covering by the corresponding bundle isomorphisms, hence hold in the sheaf. All operations commute with pullback. Since morphisms of algebraic spaces are natural transformations of their sheaves by [def-trf-algebraic-space], these operations give actual maps $P\times_SP\to P$, $S\to P$ and $P\to P$ satisfying the commutative group equations.

source.place: section-picard-functor, the Picard functor as a sheaf of abelian groups

proof.text: Test the diagonal on a scheme $T\to P\times_SP$, given by $s,t\in P(T)$. By the local representative property proved in step 3, choose an fppf covering $T_i\to T$ on which they are represented by bundles $V_i,W_i$ on $X_{T_i}$, and set $L_i=V_i\otimes W_i^\vee$. By [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], $X_{T_i}\to T_i$ remains proper, flat and of finite presentation; the structure-sheaf hypothesis persists since every $T_i$-scheme is an $S$-scheme. Apply [lem-sc-picard-diagonal-locally-closed] to this morphism and the rank-one bundle $L_i$. It gives an immersion $Z_i\to T_i$ of finite presentation, universal for the pullback of $L_i$ to come from a finite locally free module $N$ on the test base. Such $N$ necessarily has rank one. Indeed, over any residue field $k$ the structure-sheaf hypothesis gives $H^0(X_k,\mathcal O)=k\ne0$, so $X_k$ is nonempty. At a point above that residue field, $f^*N\simeq L_i$ forces the rank of $N$ to be one. By [lem-pc-pic-exact], coming from such an invertible $N$ is equivalent to $[L_i]=0$ in the relative Picard sheaf. Thus $Z_i$ represents the equality functor of $s|_{T_i}$ and $t|_{T_i}$ on all test schemes, including nonreduced ones.

source.place: Tag 0D2D, lemma-diagonal-pic, last paragraph; more-morphisms.tex Tag 0BDP, lemma-diagonal-picard-flat-proper; pic.tex Tag 0B9M

proof.text: The equality functor $E=T\times_{P\times_SP}P$ is already an algebraic space because $P$ is one. Its pullback to $T_i$ is represented by $Z_i$. Each $Z_i\to T_i$ is a quasi-compact immersion, since it is an immersion of finite presentation. Apply [lem-sfb-space-quasi-compact-immersion-locality] to $E\to T$ and the fppf covering $\{T_i\to T\}$. It follows that $E\to T$ is an immersion, including representability by a scheme. Every scheme test of the diagonal has this form. Hence the diagonal of $P\to S$ is representable by immersions, as asserted.

lean.note: The existing Type (u+1)-valued relative Picard group functor is identified with the universe lift of a commutative-group-valued functor whose underlying sheaf is the algebraic space P. Properness supplies quasi-compactness and separatedness, hence quasi-separatedness, so local finite presentation of f is its full finite-presentation hypothesis. Local finite presentation of P/S is tested on all representable etale scheme charts.
